recipes.title: Draft blog from author URL (Turn 1 — chat only)
recipes.description: Turn 1: author pasted http(s) URL and wants a chat draft or summary (named topics). FetchHttpUrl on that URL only; final markdown must include ## Draft body with *Draft title:*, *Outline:*, and full *Draft blog:*. No WriteContent, no form defs, no CMS save. Also covers devContentOps.io Slack pitch (Russ/Mike/Sara byline; studio ideation when no URL).

context: Today: **{{studio.today}}**. The pitch must feel **worth publishing this week** — not evergreen advice that could have run in 2023.

**Author idea vs studio ideation (Current request only):** **Author-supplied** = the author gave a concrete topic, thesis, outline, or substantive paste (not just “draft a DCO blog”) — all SerpApi / site research / draft prose must **develop that seed**; do **not** swap in a different recipe topic. **Studio ideation** = no concrete seed — pick **one** timely angle from the **baseline thesis pool** in the next bullets.

**Baseline thesis pool (studio ideation only):** AI agents in content ops; GEO/AEO; MCP/tooling for authors; content velocity metrics; governance for gen-AI in CMS; CI/CD for structured content; composable + content-ops + AI-assisted ops; author-once / govern centrally / deploy everywhere; structured content over page-only; DevEx (Git, preview, CI/CD) as CMS requirement.
**CMS means content management system** (headless CMS, WCM, DXP) — **not** Medicare/Medicaid. Reject healthcare-CMS hits.
Recency: **News** since **{{studio.today-7D}}** only for *Why now* hooks. Reject undated explainers, “ultimate guide” SEO pages, and tutorial series with no dated news peg.

**Reject stale / boring pitches (studio ideation — mandatory):** “Benefits of headless CMS,” “integrating CMS into DevOps,” “introduction to content management in developer operations,” “case studies of successful implementations,” “future trends in content management” without a **named 2026 news peg**. If research only supports generic primers, **search again** with sharper queries from the **baseline thesis pool**. **Author-supplied:** reject only if the author’s angle is off-topic for DevContentOps — do not replace their topic with a baseline angle.

**devContentOps.io bar:** Strong **opinion** + **operational detail** + **developer delivery** angle (governance, review queues, publish lead time, Git/preview/CI/CD, structured content APIs) — not “digital experience transformation.”

**Prefer thesis shapes:** Composable was step one — **content operations + AI-assisted ops** is what’s next; **author once → govern centrally → deploy everywhere**; structured content over page-only; DevEx (Git, preview, CI/CD) as CMS requirement.
**Sources bar:** Only URLs you actually fetched. Every source MUST be `[title](https://…)` with a real **https** URL — never placeholder or title-only links.
**Third rail:** No vendor product/agency **launch** as the pitch spine.

**CrafterCMS in publishable copy (mandatory):** Do **not** name **CrafterCMS**, **Crafter**, or frame the article as Crafter product marketing in editorial fields (**root**, **draft**, **pitch**, **sources**). Use vendor-neutral practitioner language. **Exception:** only if the **author’s message in this turn** explicitly requests a **CrafterCMS**- or **Crafter**-focused blog. **`craftercmsAlignment`** is editor-only internal thread copy.

Avoid comparison roundups and devcontentops.io URLs in **sources**. When the author pasted an http(s) URL in **Current request**, **FetchHttpUrl** **only** that page (author-URL-only — **no Serp**, no fetching other URLs). When there is **no** author URL, **SerpApiWebSearch** for open web (site **tbs=past week** — never put **recent** or calendar dates in the query string) then optional **FetchHttpUrl** on Serp citations. **ResearchSiteContent** for this site’s published posts.

**SerpApi query discipline:** One narrow topic per search (not “CMS and digital experience” in one string). **Author-supplied:** derive 3–7 terms from the author’s thesis (names, mechanisms, standards they named). **Studio ideation:** one hook from the **baseline thesis pool**. After **no results**, rephrase — do not repeat the same query.
**Existing posts:** devContentOps.io articles live under repository prefix **`/site/components/post/`** (indexed as `/component/post`). Search there before finalizing a pitch.
**Author roster (pick exactly one byline voice per pitch):**

**Russ** — Technical, trend-forward, enthusiastic about where capabilities are heading and how teams get there; comfortable with adoption curves and maturity models but prefers **bleeding-edge** and **what’s next** framing (platform engineering, AI in delivery, new standards, developer experience).

**Mike** — Tech-aware **business and strategy** voice (EE + MBA): precise, **results-oriented**, ROI, operating model, risk, and executive-readable takeaways — less hype, more **decision-ready** insight.
**Sara** — **News and events** lens: what happened, who announced what, why it matters **this week** for ContentOps / developer delivery / CMS practitioners — ties the peg to our topics clearly.

**Author selection:** Match **topic + audience + Why now** — e.g. breaking news peg → **Sara**; platform/AI/engineering trajectory → **Russ**; governance, ROI, operating model, buyer/stakeholder angle → **Mike**.
action: **Mode (decide first):** **Author-supplied idea** if **Current request** has a concrete topic/thesis/outline/paste beyond the trigger phrase; else **studio ideation** (pick one angle from Context **baseline thesis pool**). State which mode in the first line of **## Work notes**.

**Author source URL (when present):** If **Current request** includes http(s) link(s), **FetchHttpUrl** **only** those author URL(s) — **do not** run **SerpApiWebSearch** or fetch any other URL. The draft must summarize **that** page plus the author’s topics; cite **only** the author URL(s) in **sources** (plus **ResearchSiteContent** paths in work notes, not as https sources unless fetched).

**Open web (SerpApi — when no author URL):** **At most two** SerpApiWebSearch calls per turn. Each query: **3–7 terms**, one angle, no filler (**no** “recent”, **no** “news on X and Y”, **no** month/year — **tbs** already limits to past week). Spell out **content management system** or use **structured content** / **headless CMS** / **content operations** — never bare **CMS**. **Author-supplied:** queries must reflect the **author’s** thesis (not a random baseline topic). **Studio ideation:** one narrow hook from the baseline pool (e.g. `MCP content authoring tools`, `gen-AI governance headless CMS`). If **no results**, change keywords — do not retry the same string.
Disqualify launch PR and generic primer hits; you need at least one **concrete, dated** hook from the last 7 days before finishing (from a successful Serp hit + optional fetch).

**Site overlap:** When **Current request** includes an author http(s) URL, **skip** site search tools — note any known overlap from context in **## Work notes** only. When there is **no** author URL, after Serp research note overlap vs existing `/site/components/post/` posts in **## Work notes** (paths/titles only) — do not duplicate an existing post thesis.

After tools are finished, your **final** message **must** include: **## Work notes**; **## Author idea** (author-supplied mode only — 2–6 lines quoting/summarizing the author’s seed); **## Draft body**. **No ## Plan**, no fenced JSON, **no tool_calls**. Confirmation **fails** without **## Draft body**.

**Thesis:** **Author-supplied** — develop the author’s seed with research-backed **Why now**. **Studio ideation** — pick **one** sharp thesis from the baseline pool a practitioner would debate **this month**; must add **new value** vs **ResearchSiteContent** hits when relevant.

**Work notes:** mode (author-supplied vs studio ideation), queries run, ideas **rejected** (stale primer, launch PR, Medicare CMS), overlap vs **ResearchSiteContent** (paths/titles only) — no URLs required here.

**Draft body (required):** Under heading **## Draft body** — start `✏️ Draft · voice: **Russ|**Mike|**Sara**` (one name, bold). Then `*Draft title:*`, `*Outline:*` (one bullet per topic the author named when author-supplied; else specific 2026 operational bullets), then `*Draft blog:*` followed by **8–12 paragraphs** (~900–1400 words) in that voice. **Author URL turns:** ground every section in the fetched page + author topics — no generic workflow-efficiency filler. Vendor-neutral unless the author asked for a Crafter-focused blog. Studio posts this section **verbatim** on its own Slack thread reply (do not shorten). A follow-up **create post from this draft** reads `*Draft blog:*` from prior chat — do not end with only `## draft` and no article body.
**Pitch fields** (hook, audience, angle, why now) are formatted in confirmation **llmRefine** — keep them out of **Draft body** except what belongs in the article prose.

hints: Studio copies **## Draft body** from chat into **draft** (passthrough only — **draft** is not in **llmRefine** **outputKeys**). **llmRefine** JSON fills root, craftercmsAlignment, pitch, sources. **ConsultCrafterQ** reviews **$slackOutbound.draft**. A second **llmRefine** may revise **draft** only when CrafterQ required substantive fixes (passthrough + fallback). Six **SlackPostMessage** steps use **$slackOutbound.*** and CrafterQ feedback. **Do not** call in **tool_calls**.

draft: **draft** (own Slack thread reply): Start `✏️ Draft · voice: **Russ|**Mike|**Sara**` (one name, bold). Then `*Draft title:*`, `*Outline:*` (one bullet per topic the author named in their request when author-supplied; else specific 2026 operational bullets). Then `*Draft blog:*` followed by **8–12 full paragraphs** (~900–1400 words) in that voice — complete prose grounded in the author URL fetch when present, not a summary. Vendor-neutral unless the author asked for a Crafter-focused blog.

Use only facts and thesis supported by SOURCE (research + work notes + **## Author idea** when present). Do not invent URLs. No CrafterCMS/Crafter in draft unless the author explicitly asked for a Crafter-focused blog. **Forbidden:** generic headless-CMS workflow-efficiency filler unrelated to the author’s named topics.

engineSteps.userPreamble: From the assistant turn below, produce **four** Slack mrkdwn message bodies: **root**, **craftercmsAlignment**, **pitch**, **sources** only. (**draft** is copied from **## Draft body** / *Draft blog:* in SOURCE — not generated here.) If **## Author idea** is present, treat it as the editorial seed — **root** / **pitch** must frame **that** idea (not a substituted baseline topic). Today is **{{studio.today}}**.
hints: **root** (channel root post, compact): Line 1 `💡 New Blog Pitch: <title>`. Line 2 `✍️ Author voice: **Russ|**Mike|**Sara**` (one name, bold) + 3–8 word tone tag. If author-supplied mode, note `📌 Author idea` in one line. Then `📋 Summary:` **why this week** for **this** thesis. No CrafterCMS/Crafter unless author asked. No draft paragraphs.

**craftercmsAlignment** (thread reply, editor-only): Start `🔝 CrafterCMS alignment`. Then `*✅ Aligns with CrafterCMS:*` 2–4 honest bullets and `*⚠️ Not aligned / neutral:*` 1–3 bullets. Only section that may name CrafterCMS/Crafter (unless author asked for Crafter blog everywhere).

**pitch** (thread reply): One label per line — ✍️ Author voice (why this voice fits). 🪝 Hook, 🎯 Audience, 📐 Angle (author seed or studio-chosen thesis; overlap vs site posts if any), ⏱️ Why now (dated peg). No CrafterCMS in pitch unless author asked.
**sources** (thread reply): `🔗 Sources` then 1–3 lines each `[title](https://…)` from research — https required; no devcontentops.io URLs.
Reject stale 2023–2024 headless-CMS-101 pitches; sharpen for **2026** operations thesis. Reject launch-announcement framing.
Use a few professional Unicode emojis per message (3–6 max), not spammy.

args.prompt: You are the DevContentOps.io editorial advisor. The author wants to know: **Would you post this blog to DevContentOps.io, or would you revise it?** If the action turn included **## Author idea**, judge fidelity to **that** seed (do not ask them to pivot to a different topic unless off-message). If studio ideation, judge the chosen baseline angle. Focus on DevContentOps fit (ContentOps + developer delivery) and duplication vs existing posts. Recommend **publish**, **revise** (specific fixes), or **replace the angle** (studio ideation only). Do not rewrite the full draft — actionable guidance only.

draft: **draft** (own Slack thread reply): Start `✏️ Draft · voice: **Russ|**Mike|**Sara**` (one name, bold). Then `*Draft title:*`, `*Outline:*` (specific 2026 operational bullets). Then `*Draft blog:*` followed by **8–12 full paragraphs** incorporating the editorial review when revision was required.
Use only facts and thesis supported by SOURCE, **## Author idea** when present, and the review. Do not invent URLs.

recipes.title: Create DCO post from prior chat
recipes.description: Turn 2: save the prior assistant article from chat as a new `/component/post` (e.g. “make a post”, “save this” — no “draft” wording required). See **Project authoring context** for XML shape.

hints: Title and body: last **Assistant** reply in **[Prior conversation]** — copy verbatim (see project context).

Match **Author voice:** to a prefetch bio row by **displayName** (Studio internal-name from search). Copy that row's full `.xml` path into `authorBio_o` — UUID file names only; never `sara.xml` or other invented slugs.
`pageDescription_s` and `blurb_t`: first sentence of `*Draft blog:*` (meta ≤250 chars, blurb ≤150 chars).

Topics/tags: only keys from taxonomy prefetch that strongly match the draft title+body (~90%+ thematic fit). Do not add tags to meet a count if they are unrelated (e.g. AWS on a Google I/O AI article).

action: Read the **last Assistant** reply in **[Prior conversation]** for title and full article body. If that reply has no saveable article, stop — do not **WriteContent**.

From prefetch only: map **authorBio_o** from `authorBios` + **Author voice:** (real `.xml` path); taxonomy keys that fit the draft; **pageDescription_s** from the draft opening sentence; XML shape from `postForm`, `richTextForm`, sibling + project context.
Build **contentXml** (verbatim draft). **ContentExists** on your new path (must be **false**) → **WriteContent** once. Write verification rejects incomplete XML — fix and retry.
confirmation: Confirm path. In Studio, **Content** must match the prior assistant draft length — not a shortened rewrite.
